text: I often overthink even small decisions.
agree: You report revisiting even small decisions.
disagree: You do not identify with frequent overthinking of small decisions.
tip: For a small decision, list two workable options and choose a reasonable stopping point.

text: I feel more energized when I’m around people than when I’m alone.
agree: You describe social time as more energizing than time alone.
disagree: Social time may not feel more energizing than time alone for you.
tip: Notice which kinds of company and quiet time leave you feeling restored.

text: I prefer to finish one task completely before starting another.
agree: You prefer completing one task before switching.
disagree: You do not have a strong preference for finishing one task before starting another.
tip: Try a short focused work period and notice whether switching tasks helps or interrupts you.

text: Criticism affects me more than I show to others.
agree: You report that criticism has an impact you do not fully show.
disagree: You do not identify with hiding the impact of criticism.
tip: Separate the useful part of feedback from its delivery; ask for a concrete example when needed.

text: I trust my gut feeling more than logic when making important choices.
agree: You describe a preference for intuition in important choices.
disagree: You do not describe intuition as more trusted than logic.
tip: For an important choice, compare your first impression with the available facts.

text: I find it hard to say "no" even when I’m busy.
agree: You report difficulty declining requests when busy.
disagree: You do not identify with difficulty declining requests when busy.
tip: Before accepting a request, check your time and consider a realistic alternative.

text: I learn better from my mistakes than from my successes.
agree: You see mistakes as especially useful learning experiences.
disagree: You do not see mistakes as better teachers than successes.
tip: Look at one success and one mistake: what can each teach you about your next attempt?

text: I need a plan for almost everything to feel calm.
agree: You describe planning as important to feeling calm.
disagree: You do not describe needing a plan for almost everything to feel calm.
tip: Try a short plan that leaves room for one unexpected change.

text: I care a lot about what people think of me.
agree: You report that other people’s opinions matter a lot to you.
disagree: You do not identify strongly with caring about other people’s opinions.
tip: Ask whose feedback is relevant to this situation and which values matter to you.

text: I would rather be respected than be popular.
agree: You choose respect over popularity in this comparison.
disagree: You do not choose respect over popularity in this comparison; that does not mean respect is unimportant.
tip: Describe what respectful treatment looks like to you in a real relationship.

text: I get motivated more by challenges than by rewards.
agree: You describe challenges as more motivating than rewards.
disagree: You do not describe challenges as more motivating than rewards.
tip: Experiment with a manageable challenge and a small reward to see what helps you start.

text: I keep my emotions to myself instead of sharing them.
agree: You describe tending to keep emotions private.
disagree: You do not identify with generally keeping emotions to yourself.
tip: Consider when privacy serves you and when sharing with someone you trust might be useful.

text: I believe failure is the best way to grow.
agree: You view failure as a particularly important route to growth.
disagree: You do not view failure as the best route to growth.
tip: Name one lesson you can learn from practice, feedback or a successful experience too.

text: I feel uncomfortable in a group if I don’t know what to do.
agree: You report discomfort in groups when your role is unclear.
disagree: You do not identify with discomfort in groups specifically because your role is unclear.
tip: If a group task is unclear, ask what is expected or offer one small contribution.

text: I would choose honesty over kindness if I had to pick one.
agree: You choose honesty when the statement asks you to prioritize one value.
disagree: You do not choose honesty over kindness in this comparison; that does not imply dishonesty.
tip: Think of wording that is both truthful and considerate; real situations often allow both.
